title: scheduler: TPGroup state machine + quarantine-aware dispatch (no new work on unhealthy groups)
author: Marcus Reed
description:
Context: We have a class of TP hangs/timeouts where a TP worker group stops making forward progress but the scheduler continues to route work to it. This PR introduces an explicit TPGroup health/state model in the scheduler and makes dispatch quarantine-aware so we do not schedule new requests onto known-bad groups. This is a prerequisite for watchdog-triggered quarantine and controlled teardown (PRs to follow) and provides immediate blast-radius reduction when a group is detected as unhealthy.

What changed (high level): Add TPGroupState state machine to scheduler: HEALTHY -> DEGRADED -> QUARANTINED -> DRAINING/RESETTING (internal) with explicit transition rules. Persist per-group health in scheduler registry keyed by (host_id, tp_group_id). Gate dispatch: scheduler will not assign new work to QUARANTINED/RESETTING groups; it will instead pick another compatible group or fail fast with a retriable error when no healthy capacity exists. Add metrics hooks (counters + gauges) for state transitions and dispatch skips. Add unit tests for: quarantine prevents assignment; transition ordering; race where group becomes quarantined between candidate selection and enqueue; and fairness behavior when some groups are unavailable.

Why it helps: When a single rank stalls, collectives may hang indefinitely and that TP group becomes a black hole for requests. By quarantining at the group level and ensuring the scheduler respects that, we stop piling on work, reduce customer-visible timeouts, and create a clean boundary for recovery actions (restart/quarantine TTL).

Implementation details: New enum TPGroupState { HEALTHY, DEGRADED, QUARANTINED, RESETTING } stored in TpGroupRegistry. Scheduler dispatch path now consults TpGroupRegistry::is_schedulable(group) and records a skip reason when not schedulable. Quarantine is sticky until explicitly cleared by reset completion (to be wired up by watchdog PR). Added a lightweight atomic “epoch” to avoid the TOCTOU race: candidate selection captures group_epoch and enqueue validates epoch unchanged; if changed to quarantined, reselect.

Metrics: runtime.scheduler.tp_group_state{state=...} gauge per host; runtime.scheduler.tp_group_state_transition_total{from,to,reason}; runtime.scheduler.dispatch_skipped_total{reason=quarantined|resetting|no_healthy_group}; runtime.scheduler.candidate_reselect_total{reason=epoch_changed}.

Notes / follow-ups: This PR does not yet introduce the watchdog; it only provides the scheduler primitives and hard gating behavior. Next PR will mark groups QUARANTINED based on forward-progress watchdog + collective async error propagation and will implement RESETTING lifecycle.

Testing: Unit tests added under scheduler/ tests; ran local stress sim with forced quarantine to verify dispatch reroutes. CI includes scheduler-unit and runtime-integration (no GPU).

Rollout: No behavior change unless a group is marked QUARANTINED/RESETTING (currently only via admin test hook). Safe to land ahead of watchdog changes.
commits: scheduler: quarantine-aware dispatch gating + reselect on epoch change
tests: TP group quarantine dispatch + transition ordering

conversation:
Sofia Ivanova (review): The dispatch gating looks good, but I’m worried about the race between candidate selection and enqueue. If the group flips to QUARANTINED after selection, we may still enqueue and then rely on downstream checks. Can we make this deterministic?

Marcus Reed (author): Good call. I added an epoch value to the registry; selection captures (group_id, epoch) and enqueue revalidates. If epoch changed or state not schedulable, we reselect and increment a metric (runtime.scheduler.candidate_reselect_total{reason=epoch_changed}). Added a unit test that flips quarantine between select/enqueue.

Noah Patel (review): State model: do we need DEGRADED in this PR? It’s not used for gating currently.

Marcus Reed (author): Keeping DEGRADED as a non-gating state for now so we can surface “slow but progressing” separately from QUARANTINED once watchdog lands. It also helps avoid a binary view in dashboards. Dispatch currently only gates QUARANTINED/RESETTING.

Rafael Mendes (review): From SRE perspective, please ensure we have a metric that tells us when scheduler refuses to place work due to quarantine (and reason). Also consider an error code that the router can treat as retriable.

Marcus Reed (author): Added dispatch_skipped_total with reason labels and a new internal status code TP_GROUP_UNAVAILABLE mapped to 503 retriable upstream. Also added log line at INFO (rate-limited) when no healthy group exists for a placement attempt.

Julian Moore (review): Minor: metric cardinality—transition reason should be bounded. Please avoid using raw error strings.

Marcus Reed (author): Updated to enum TransitionReason with a small set (watchdog, async_error, admin, reset_complete, unknown). No raw strings.

Sofia Ivanova (final review): Approved. Please add a brief comment documenting sticky quarantine semantics and how it’s cleared.

Marcus Reed (author): Added comment in tp_group_registry.cc and in header docs.

Merge: Squash merge after green CI.
